title: Power Windows and Rear Window Defrost: What the Controls Do
introduction: I start with the body style, because convertible window features differ from the standard arrangement. This overview explains which switches command which windows, how to request one-touch operation where fitted, and how rear window defrost helps visibility. It is a guide to system behavior; it does not provide access, repair or diagnostic-test instructions.

edits.text: Power Windows: Controls and Automatic Operation
NOTE: Convertible models have neither one-touch up nor bounce back features.
edits.why: I check this body-style exception before interpreting window behavior: those features are absent on a convertible, so their absence alone is not a malfunction.

edits.text: Standard power window features include one-touch up/down operation for the door windows only, with the convertible exception noted above. To request one-touch operation, momentarily press the master window control switch (or passenger door window control switch) to the second detent, then release it.
edits.why: The second detent is the switch position that requests automatic movement. Think of it as handing the window a brief instruction instead of supervising the button throughout its travel. This door-window feature description does not extend one-touch operation to the rear quarter windows.

edits.text: Use the master window control switch to raise or lower either the driver or passenger door window. The passenger door window can also be raised or lowered using the passenger door window control switch.
edits.why: The passenger glass has two named control options. I keep that distinction in mind when learning the controls: the master switch commands either door window, while the passenger switch commands the passenger window.

edits.text: On convertible models, use the master window control switch to raise or lower the rear quarter windows.
edits.why: The convertible adds rear quarter glass to the windows commanded by the master switch. That expands which windows it controls without establishing an automatic operating mode for them.

edits.text: Rear Window Defrost: Heating the Glass
Activating rear window defrost energizes the rear window defrost grid. The energized grid warms the glass to improve rearward visibility.
edits.why: I picture the grid as a heating blanket for the rear glass: electrical energy supplies the warmth, and improved rearward visibility is the intended result. This overview does not specify activation controls, heating time or a performance test.
